BACKGROUND. This repo produces a two-person video podcast. Every episode begins as four separate WebM files from a Daily.co room: host camera audio, host camera video, guest camera audio, guest camera video. They do not share a zero. In the reference episode the host tracks start at 0.225s and the guest tracks at 224.875s because the guest joined 224.7 seconds late. Tracks also contain dropouts, meaning stretches where packets stopped arriving: host audio has one 76.860s hole at 151.859s and host video has thirteen holes totalling 219.960s including a 203.887s frozen stretch.

THE PROBLEM. The pipeline computes episode timing in three incompatible ways and nothing compares them: container header start times (used by the composite), first-packet PTS (the correct master grid), and a 13-digit epoch parsed out of the filename (used by the transcript). Five consecutive renders shipped broken as a result.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS CORRECT. server/pipeline/av_sync.py derive_timeline() computes ONE session grid with T=0 at the earliest packet across all four tracks, measures every dropout as a packet hole, and build_stems() renders four stems that are all exactly the same length on that grid, HOLDING every dropout as silence or a frozen frame rather than deleting it. It writes timeline.json describing the grid, each track's grid offset, and every hole. Measured: all four stems within 4ms of each other, session length 2842.196s.

THE RULE, ratified by the owner: no stage may remove time from one track without removing it from all four, and dropouts are HELD at every size rather than cut.

THIS RUNG makes the grid the single coordinate system. Your lane is one piece of that.

CRITICAL DESIGN CONSTRAINT, applies to every lane in this batch: your change must be PURELY ADDITIVE. Add a grid-aware path alongside the existing one, default it OFF, and leave every current caller behaving exactly as it does today. A later step wires the orchestrator to turn the new paths on together. If your change alters current default behavior, the test suite goes red and the batch cannot integrate. Additive means: new keyword argument defaulting to the old behavior, or a new function beside the old one. Never rip out the old path.

A SECOND CONSTRAINT THAT HAS ALREADY CAUSED A BUG HERE: the stems ALREADY CONTAIN their leading placement. Each stem was rendered with its grid offset baked in as leading silence or padding. So when a consumer reads stems, every per-track placement offset must be ZERO. Passing a grid_offset into a consumer that reads stems applies the delay twice. This exact double-shift is documented in av_sync.py as a bug that already shipped once on this episode.

YOUR LANE: make the master timeline content-addressed, and stop a third participant being silently dropped.

1. CONTENT PIN. timeline.json currently describes the grid but nothing binds it to the stems it describes. If a stem is rebuilt or replaced, a stale timeline still looks valid. Add a content pin: a hash over the four stem files (size and a content digest are both acceptable, state which you chose and why) recorded in timeline.json when write_timeline runs, plus a verification function that takes a timeline and a stems directory and reports whether the pin still matches. The verifier must distinguish three cases and say which: matches, mismatched (a stem changed), and missing (a stem is absent or the timeline predates pinning). Missing is not a pass.

2. TRACKS THAT ARE CURRENTLY THROWN AWAY. classify_track_filenames has two problems.

   (a) It uses `labels = ["host", "guest"]` and a zip, so a recording with three PARTICIPANTS silently drops the third person's tracks and the pipeline proceeds as if they were never there. Make that a loud failure naming how many participants were detected and which were dropped. Two participants must keep working exactly as today, and a solo recording must keep working if it does today, so check the current behavior before you change the arity rule.

   (b) Its docstring says screen-share tracks are IGNORED, and they are. The owner does screen shares and wants them usable. A screen share is not a third participant: it is an additional VIDEO source belonging to an existing participant, with its own start time and its own dropouts. Classify screen tracks into their own role rather than discarding them, count PARTICIPANTS by camera-audio tracks only so a screen share never trips the arity guard, and carry screen tracks through derive_timeline so they receive a grid offset and a hole list exactly like any other track and appear in timeline.json.

   Scope limit for THIS lane: classify and place screen tracks on the grid, and include them in the timeline. Do NOT build screen stems or change any renderer; later work owns that. Prove with a test that a track set containing a screen share is classified correctly, lands on the grid, and does not trip the participant guard.

Additive: existing callers of write_timeline and derive_timeline must keep working unchanged. Do not edit orchestrator.py, video_assembly.py, angle_render.py or interview_transcription.py; other workers own those in parallel.

THE RED REQUIREMENT. Every check or guard you add must be PROVEN CAPABLE OF FAILING. Write a test that feeds the poisoned or wrong input and asserts it blocks or raises. A test proving only that the happy path works is worthless here: this codebase shipped five broken releases green because eight gates could report success without measuring anything. In your summary, list each guard you added and the exact poisoned input that makes it fail.

Put the mode and the timeline identity into the cache key, and prove with a test that a raw-built cache entry is rejected for a stems-mode request.

THE DEFECT, measured on the reference episode and not hypothetical. This module builds its own zero by parsing a 13-digit epoch out of each source filename (near interview_transcription.py:314 and :352) and adding that flat offset to the speech engine's local times (near :439 and :455). It has NO model of dropouts. The host's raw audio decodes to 2765.311s because its 76.86s hole collapses during decode, so every host timestamp after 151.859s is up to 76.86 SECONDS early. Measured proof: the host's last transcript segment ends at 2761.45s against a session length of 2842.196s, and seven host segments are timestamped inside the hole window, which is impossible. THE FIX: add a mode that transcribes the STEMS. Stems are hole-filled and all four are the same length on one grid, so the speech engine's local times ARE grid times and need only the grid origin applied, with no filename parsing and no per-track guessing.

Add a guard that makes the old failure detectable rather than silent: after producing timestamps for a track, compare the last timestamp against the known session length and flag a track whose transcript ends implausibly early. Make the tolerance a named constant. This is the check that would have caught an 80-second shortfall.

If a stray filename does not match the expected pattern the current code silently leaves that track's offset at 0.0. In the new mode that must not be possible.
